concepts.title: Bharat and India: Names Across Time

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Bharat and India: Names Across Time' refers to.
questions.a: Our country has carried many names: Bharat, Bhāratavarsha and India, each rooted in ancient texts and usage, so that the constitution itself begins with the words, India, that is Bharat.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Bharat and India: Names Across Time'.
questions.a: Names hold memory: calling the land Bharat or India ties today's nation to millennia of history.

concepts.title: The Indian Subcontinent and Its Bounds

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Indian Subcontinent and Its Bounds' refers to.
questions.a: India sits in the Indian subcontinent, a great triangle of land walled by the Himalayas in the north, washed by the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal, and crossed by rivers such as the Indus, Sarasvati and Ganga.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Indian Subcontinent and Its Bounds'.
questions.a: Natural boundaries of mountains and seas helped a distinct civilisation grow between the Himalayas and the two seas.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Indian Subcontinent and Its Bounds' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Physical map of the subcontinent (source: fees105.txt, Physical map of the subcontinent)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Evidence from Sanchi Stupa' refers to.
questions.a: A carving on the north gate of the Great Sanchi Stupa shows a rural Indian scene of about 2,300 years ago; monuments like Sanchi are material sources that let us picture life in ancient times.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Evidence from Sanchi Stupa'.
questions.a: A stone carving is a window: the Sanchi panel preserves a day of village work from centuries ago.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Evidence from Sanchi Stupa' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'India and Its Neighbours' refers to.
questions.a: The chapter places India among its neighbours of the subcontinent and shows how land and sea routes linked the region, carrying goods and ideas in every direction for thousands of years.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'India and Its Neighbours'.
questions.a: No country lives alone: India's story is tied to the lands and waters around it.

questions.q: Under which section is 'India and Its Neighbours' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: India in the world (source: fees105.txt, India in the world)
